problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with velocity $v(t)=\frac{{t}^{2}-t}{4},$ where $t>0$ is the time. If the particle is at the position $x=-\frac{1}{6}$ when $t=2,$ calculate the position $x$ of the particle at time $t.$

feedback.worked_solution:
We start by integrating the velocity to get $x(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int \frac{6}{t}\,\text{d}t \\  & =6\operatorname{ln}⁡(t)+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C$, we use the fact that $x(1)=4.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}4 & =6\operatorname{ln}⁡(1)+C \\ 4 & =6(0)+C \\ C & =4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the position $x$ of the particle at time $t$ is 

$$
x(t)=6\operatorname{ln}⁡(t)+4.
$$
